title: Domain
description: A Domain is a thin, identity-bearing node that names a bounded context (an organization, a functional area, a subdomain). It does NOT contain primitives: membership is expressed by each primitive naming its home Domain via its `domain` reference (the authored form of the primary `belongs_to` edge). The domain hierarchy is expressed by each non-root Domain naming its `parent`; the single rootless Domain is the organization / tenant. The dot-separated `path` is a derived cache of the `parent` chain, never the authoritative source of placement.

name.description: The lowercase identifier for this domain. Unique within a document (domains are a flat set, so the name alone resolves a home reference).

description.description: A human-readable explanation of what this domain represents.

owner.description: Optional owner of this domain — the Position or Person accountable for it. Part of what gives a Domain identity independent of its members (the identity test).

parent.description: The name of this domain's parent Domain. Omitted for exactly one Domain — the organization / tenant root. The parent chain (not `path`) is the authoritative hierarchy.

path.description: DERIVED CACHE — the fully qualified dot-separated path computed from the `parent` chain, kept for naming and fast prefix filtering. Never authoritative; regenerated on re-home. Optional and may be omitted from authored documents.
